title: The star cluster Messier 7
caption: The open star cluster Messier 7, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope at La Silla
celestial: M 7, Messier 7, NGC 6475 · constellation Scorpius · about 800 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Messier 7, a bright star cluster also catalogued as NGC 6475, is the subject of this view from the Wide Field Imager at ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile. It lies about 800 light-years away, in the direction of the tail of Scorpius, the Scorpion.

Messier 7 is easy to spot with the naked eye and ranks among the most prominent open clusters in the sky. An open cluster is a loose group of stars born together from the same cloud of gas and dust and only weakly held together by gravity; over time such clusters tend to drift apart.

Because the stars of an open cluster share a common age and distance, differences between them reveal how stars of different masses evolve. That is one reason Messier 7 is an important target for research as well as an easy sight for skywatchers.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (33.11 x 32.12 arcminutes) and distance (800 light years), the frame spans roughly 7.7 × 7.5 light-years. Its light set out about 800 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image from the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope combines B, V and I filters, from visible light into the near-infrared. The colour assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Messier 7 is visible to the naked eye, but the camera's long exposures reveal many fainter stars, and the I-band light is invisible to the eye.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The image combines exposures through B, V and I filters, spanning visible light into the near-infrared. Although the cluster is plain to the naked eye, a camera on a large telescope records far fainter stars in the surrounding field.
